articles.title: What happened to Jaylen Harrell? Police reveal alleged Uber driver assault before Titans star’s crash
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell is facing questions after a serious car accident in Tampa, Florida, left him hospitalized with major
articles.body: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell is facing questions after a serious car accident in Tampa, Florida, left him hospitalized with major injuries. According to the Tampa Police Department, the 24-year-old allegedly assaulted his Uber driver while riding in the back seat on Friday morning, November 20. Police say the driver lost control after the reported incident, hitting another vehicle before crashing into a utility pole. Harrell struck his head against the windshield and lost consciousness. The incident is now under investigation, while the NFL player remains in the hospital.Tampa Police Reveal What Happened Before Jaylen Harrell's Serious Car AccidentThe accident took place on Friday morning while Harrell was travelling in a white Kia Sorento rideshare vehicle in his hometown of Tampa.According to a statement from the Tampa Police Department obtained by the Daily Mail, Harrell was sitting in the back seat when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was moving.Police said the driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved after the alleged incident. The Kia then struck another vehicle before hitting a utility pole. The impact sent Harrell forward into the windshield. He hit his head and lost consciousness.The rideshare driver suffered minor injuries and received treatment at the scene. The driver of the second vehicle, a woman in her early 50s who was driving a Toyota Highlander, escaped without injuries.Harrell, however, was taken to a nearby hospital with serious injuries. Police said he remained under medical care. The department has not shared further details about his condition or explained what may have led to the alleged assault.The investigation is still active. Police are looking into the events that took place inside the vehicle before the crash. No further details about possible charges have been confirmed.Tennessee Titans Share Update on Jaylen Harrell's Hospital ConditionThe Tennessee Titans also released a statement on Saturday, November 21, confirming that Harrell was still receiving medical care. However, the team did not mention the police allegations or provide details about what happened before the crash.The statement read:"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida."We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information."At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."The team's statement came as Harrell was already dealing with a difficult season. He has not played a single game for Tennessee in 2026 after tearing his ACL during the preseason. The injury forced the Titans to place him on season-ending injured reserve in August.Harrell joined the Titans as a seventh-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Before entering the NFL, he played college football for the Michigan Wolverines and was part of the team that won the national championship following the 2023 season.The 24-year-old appeared in all 34 regular-season games during his first two NFL seasons. He started two of those games and recorded 38 combined tackles, seven tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks and one forced fumble.His absence had already kept him away from the field this season. Now, the crash has raised further concerns about his health, while the police investigation has brought a separate issue into focus.As of Sunday, November 22, the Titans had not announced any further update on Harrell's condition. The team has also not publicly addressed the allegations made in the police statement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "My babies": Patrick Mahomes marks a heartwarming milestone with Brittany Mahomes and their three children amid the win against the Cardinals
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback, had his pregnant wife, Brittany Mahomes, and their three children by his side as he led the team to
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback, had his pregnant wife, Brittany Mahomes, and their three children by his side as he led the team to a 34-7 to win against the Arizona Cardinals. Amid this, the star quarterback shared a heartwarming moment with his children that has made many emotional.Patrick Mahomes prioritises his three children and Brittany Mahomes at the clash against the Arizona CardinalsIn a clip posted by the Kansas City Chiefs and later shared by Birttany Mahomes, Patrick Mahomes is spotted running to the sidelines as his three children start jumping at the sight of him.A few seconds later, Patrick Mahomes is seen sharing a kiss with them and also his wife, Brittany Mahomes, as he then runs back to the field.The caption of the post reads as, “What it’s all about 🥹🥹🥹” as Brittany mahomes added the words, “My babies to it”.The moment has made many emotional, considering how Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, are also gearing up for the arrival of their fourth baby in just a couple of months.To make it more special, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes also received one more good news yesterday when the team they co-own, the Kansas City Current, ended up winning the NWSL championship for the first time.Though the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Patrick Mahomes could not be at the venue as he remained busy preparing for the clash against the Arizona Cardinals, his wife, Brittany Mahomes, was spotted on the field as she seemed ecstatic.In a heartwarming social media post, Brittany Mahomes wrote, “City of CHAMPIONS!! Could not be more proud of this team and this entire organization! #KCBABY 🩵❤️”Patrick Mahomes focuses on facing the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving nightFor now, the focus remains on the Kansas City Chiefs as they are all set to face the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night.After the win against the Arizona Cardinals, Patrick Mahomes opened up about it as he said, “I'm excited for the rest of the season but it all begins Thursday night.”The Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid also reflected on it as he added, “That comes from the locker room. The senior leadership,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. “They understand where we're at in the season. Every game counts. They hear it from the coaches, but hearing it from your peers is important. They don't let anything slide.”Interestingly, the Arizona Cardinals’ head coach Mike LaFleur also opened up about losing to the Kansas City Chiefs as he said, “It’s been one helluva stretch for us. It’s been one helluva stretch really since Week 2…We’ve done some good, but more bad. But we have six weeks left.”At this point in time, all eyes remain on the Kansas City Chiefs as the team gears up for Thursday night.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL defends incomplete pass ruling on Parker Washington's would-be TD in Jaguars' loss at Giants
articles.summary: (AP) — Parker Washington thought he caught the ball for a crucial touchdown in the fourth quarter, and Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen was confident eno...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. (AP) — Parker Washington thought he caught the ball for a crucial touchdown in the fourth quarter, and Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen was confident enough that he challenged the initial call of an incomplete pass.

The league defended its decision after the Jaguars lost 23-18 at the New York Giants on Sunday, ruling that Washington did not complete the catch.

"It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds," vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth told a pool reporter. "He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch."

Coen relayed that he was told "the ball switched hands.

"That was what it came down to," Coen said.

Washington felt good about possession but also did not want to blame the defeat on the officiating.

"I saw it on the Jumbotron or whatever we call it," Washington said. "It didn't go our way. You can't hang your head on that. We've got to move on and get ready for the next play."

Trevor Lawrence, who threw two interceptions while under pressure for much of the game, similarly did not want to lament the impact of the would-be touchdown on the result.

"It's a close play," Lawrence said. "Obviously, they called it and said it wasn't. It's tough. I thought it was incredible that he gave us a shot there and he caught it, and it looked like he had two feet down, but it was close. You can't leave in the refs' hands. I think it's a tough call for them."

CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore, who was an official in the league for 15 years, disagreed with the decision .

"I still had the right foot down as he's falling," Steratore said on the broadcast. "I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think he lost possession of the football."

Giants coach John Harbaugh was fine with it, saying he thought simply "the ball moved."
